To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most frequent O157:H7 STEC strains isolated from humans between 1993-1996 in Argentina, Australia or New Zealand differed from one another in terms of stxA-genotype and phagetype.
the stx genotypes and phage types of O157 STEC isolates from Argentina, Australia and NZ differ from each other, and that no common PFGE types were found.

Shiga toxin-producing E. coli O:157 strains isolated in three countries were different in terms of their Shiga toxin genotype and phage type, and no common PFGE pattern was found in strains isolated from the three countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genetic basis of the virulence of Shiga toxin (Stx)-producing Escherichia Coli (STEC).
the epidemiology, pathogenesis and evolution of Shigatoxin-producing Escherichiae (STEC), a major cause of foodborne illness in developed countries, particularly in children.

the characterisation of STEC O 157 strains isolated between January 1993 and December 1996 from patients with haemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), bloody diarrhoea, non-bloody diarrhea or unspecified conditions in Argentina, Australia or New Zealand.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the STEC strains isolated from humans from Argentina and Australia were different from the New Zealand strains in terms of stax genotype, phage type and clonal relatedness.
the O157 strains from the three countries are different from each other.
the strains of E. coli O:157:H7 isolated from patients with HUS, NBD and BD in Argentina, Australia or New Zealand, are phenotypically and genotypically different.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are no hypervirulent clones of O157:H7 in Argentina, New Zealand and Australia, but there is a need for more studies to be done on the other serogroups of STEC in Argentina and New Zealand.
the STEC O157 isolates from Argentina, Australia and NZ are not closely related to each other.
the STEC O157/H7 strains isolated in the countries studied were not identical and that they were not clonally related.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for international collaboration in the surveillance of STEC O:157 strains.
there are significant genetic differences between STEC O157 isolates from humans in Argentina and Australia.
the most prevalent stx genotype in Argentinian strains was stx2/stxc (vh-a).
